issues.cell: Part L *commit* (adj l. 422-432: 'at generation, a regeneration and a village derivation each stage') x law 2 (c)'s paths (adj l. 561-579: by hand refused; at generation, a regeneration and a village derivation the stage's rung, F-V-RAISED at a village; at an epoch and in a replay the op waits) x V07 §3.12a (3) (a village refounded in a replay epoch, the village product generating the new settlement there, VS3's palisade by V07 §3.4) x V07 §3.11's absorb half (a dossier wall record the port absorbs with no epoch builds a palisade by drawWall in VS3's form) x *the band*'s 'a village kind's drawWall, by hand or for a dossier wall record'
issues.claim: Law 2 (c) and *commit* read the outcome and a commit's bounds from the path, and two events fit two paths or none. (1) A village refounding (V07 §3.12a (3)) runs a village derivation inside a replay epoch of the creation prefix; its VS3 palisade meeting the former city's standing (neglected) aqueduct with no lawful shape takes F-V-RAISED (re-laid once with law 1's exclusions impassable and VS3's widened reach, else omitted, W_RAISED_MEETING; law 1 at each VS stage end) as a village derivation, or 'waits that epoch' (walls.waited; law 1 at the epoch's end) as a replay - and no later village epoch retries it ('a village never gains a ring at an epoch', V07 l. 2361, 2552). (2) A dossier wall record the port absorbs at a village rung with no epoch lays its palisade by drawWall in VS3's form (V07 l. 2276-2282, 2472): it is no hand edit, no epoch and no derivation, so law 2 (c) gives nothing it can take - 'refused ... with the nearest lawful declarations' the port cannot do (an absorb is refused only for its routing or another settlement, V08 l. 1954-1956), 'waits that epoch' has no epoch, F-V-RAISED is a derivation's. Builders differ in kind (re-laid, omitted, never tried), each passing §5.3's row by its own reading.
issues.required_change: *Commit*, adj l. 425: 'at generation, a regeneration and a village derivation each stage (§3.3's `StageId`),' -> 'at generation, a regeneration and a village derivation each stage (§3.3's `StageId`) - a derivation an epoch runs (a village refounding, V07 §3.12a (3)) inside that epoch's commit, and a dossier event the port applies with no epoch one commit, as an edit is -,'. Law 2 (c), adj l. 563: '**At generation, a regeneration and a village derivation:**' -> '**At generation, a regeneration and a village derivation** (a village refounding inside a replay epoch, and a palisade the port lays for a dossier wall record with no epoch, among them; never refused):'. Consequences: E-S13's T110-4 (c) adds to its paths 'a village refounded by a history replay over a former CITY's aqueduct, and a village dossier's absorb with no epoch adding a wall record across a declared aqueduct - each palisade by F-V-RAISED, else omitted and reported'; E-S14 names V08's absorb milestone for the latter.

issues.cell: Part L law 2 (b) (adj l. 552-560: Tier-3 things passable, 'an unlocked building moved as its kind's are') x J148's Tier 3 x V06 §3.7.4 (2)-(3) (a contraction's cost field: an occupied footprint impassable; its strips clear only vacant, ruined or cleared buildings, else it waits, 'never forced') x V06 §3.7.1 (a circuit's land widening excepting a raised way's strip where the trace meets it) x base §4.11's built-face legality x W14 at a village epoch (a REPLACEMENT's local re-trace through a toft)
issues.claim: At an epoch, where (a) leaves a contraction (or a circuit near a raised way, or a village REPLACEMENT's local re-trace) no lawful crossing of an aqueduct but through occupied houses, (b) makes 'an unlocked building' passable and moves it 'as its kind's are' - but no epoch op moves a building (it is kept, re-let, ruined or demolished; by hand the only move is F-REDERIVE's re-cut, re-fit or demolition as fates). Two outcomes: the houses demolished with their households displaced (as the built-face legality's declared demolish or V06 §3.19 (7)'s clearing) and the contraction laid, against its own law's 'never forced'; or an occupied building has no move, (b) has no shape and the op waits (law 2 (c); V06 §3.7.4 (3)). §5.3's row passes both builds. Pass 5's verdict (adj l. 3518-3519) named this attack; no pass since has run it.
issues.required_change: Law 2 (b), adj l. 558: 'an unlocked building moved as its kind's are.' -> 'an unlocked building cleared as the op's own law clears what its strips take - by hand F-REDERIVE's fates; at an epoch only where that law clears one (a contraction never an occupied one, V06 §3.7.4 (3)), any other being no thing (b) may move.' (the passable set reading the same words). Consequence: E-S13's T110-4 (c) adds 'an epoch contraction across a standing aqueduct whose lawful crossings are flanked by occupied houses - waiting, walls.waited, no house demolished'.

issues.cell: Part L *the wall's top* (adj l. 339-341, pass 7: PRB7G-TIM-01, -GEN-03) x *the wall strips*' weld clause (adj l. 344-346: 'the band and the width there are the wider of the two walls'') x law 1 (2), (5), (7) x an on_enceinte castle's welded stretch (base l. 5594-5595, 2279; each Enceinte its own heightCm and stretchClass, base l. 2262-2263, 7710-7716; only condition, material and epoch made the town's, base l. 2509-2516) x W1 at an epoch (V06 §3.19's founding), S6 and a hand aqueduct
issues.claim: Pass 7's one term for the wall's top names one section, but between an on_enceinte castle's weld vertices one line carries the town ring's and the bailey's records, each with its own height and stretch class, and the base makes only the stretch's condition, material and epoch one. An aqueduct across the welded stretch with its channel between the two tops is over by the lower top and merged by the higher; a gate or tower under it is admitted or barred by law 1 (5) accordingly; a run under a road deck's span between the two tops is capped by law 1 (7) on one reading and not the other. *The band* beside it already decides the same place ('the wider of the two walls''); the top has no rule, so builders take the town's, the bailey's or the higher, each passing §5.3's row by its own top.
issues.required_change: *The wall strips*, adj l. 346: 'the band and the width there are the wider of the two walls'' -> 'the band and the width there are the wider, and the wall's top the higher, of the two walls''. Consequence: E-S13's T110-4 (a) adds 'an on_enceinte castle's welded stretch an aqueduct crosses with its channel between the town ring's and the bailey's tops - read by the higher top (merged), no gate or tower under it'.

issues.cell: E-D13's first cell (adj l. 2265-2267; amended only to '(1)-(11)', adj l. 2276) x the Terms' lead (adj l. 314-316, pass 7: PRB7G-LCK-04, -GEN-05) x the Summary (adj l. 148)
issues.claim: §5.3's law-1 row as E-D13 writes it reads 'each strip, zone and end the union of every standing raised way's', the reading pass 7 replaced by 'law 1 reads each one's own ... a move or search keeping a thing clear of them reads their union': a row built from it fails a lawful wall across two raised ways whose strips meet (law 1 (4) on the union) and passes a tower in a viaduct's strip under an overlapping aqueduct's clearing arch (law 1 (5) on the union). The laws govern (*The check* queries the union and states no clause), so the END is corrected.
issues.required_change: E-D13's first cell: 'its clauses (1)-(10) as the laws state them, each strip, zone and end the union of every standing raised way's (§2.7's laws' terms)' -> 'its clauses (1)-(11) as the laws state them (§2.7's laws' terms: each raised way's own)'; and the Summary's 'several raised ways their union' (adj l. 148) -> 'several raised ways each its own'.

issues.cell: R7-06 (a) and E-S0, the state sweep's C5 topple run (adj l. 1576-1577, 1716-1717) x law 2 *Entry* (adj l. 489-491) x veto 11 (adj l. 740) x E-S6's c15 aqueduct locked over the sweep (adj l. 1842-1843)
issues.claim: The sweep makes C5's second state 'on a locked raised way, which no hazard strikes ..., the same state made by the user's hand converts (a breach of both spans, then of the support)' - but a hand convert on the raised way the user locked is an op on the locked target, which *Entry* refuses (refuse.locked; veto 11: 'only an op on the locked thing itself is refused'). On E-S6's locked c15 aqueduct the state can be made neither by the topple nor by hand, so the run never holds its state.
issues.required_change: R7-06 (a) and E-S0: '- on a locked raised way, which no hazard strikes (...), the same state made by the user's hand `convert`s (a `breach` of both spans, then of the support; J146) -' -> '- on a raised way the clause locks, the state made before the lock, by the `topple` or by hand `convert`s (a `breach` of both spans, then of the support), neither a hazard nor the user's op acting on a target the user locked (§2.7's laws, law 2 *Entry*) -'.

issues.cell: E-V7-2 (adj l. 2600-2606) x V07 §3.5a (4) (V07 l. 1604-1613: 'capped beneath the standing deck at its soffit; ... a gate VS4 would make inside the raised way's under-deck strip ... moves along the trace') x law 1 (5), (7) x E-V7-1's new variant (adj l. 2590-2593; PRB7G-TIM-04's closure) x Part H's one rule (adj l. 1675-1689)
issues.claim: Pass 7 closed PRB7G-TIM-04 with a T-V7-48 variant whose palisade gate stands under the declared aqueduct's clearing arch, the REPLACEMENT waiting. V07 §3.5a (4) still caps the palisade beneath any standing deck (law 1 (7): 'an aqueduct capping none') and moves every VS4 gate out of any under-deck strip (law 1 (5) admits one under an aqueduct's clearing arch); E-V7-2 rewrites only the sentence's first clause and the hand aqueduct's, and Part H's one rule reaches END text, FIXes and appended bars, not this design text. So the fixture's gate is moved out before the REPLACEMENT runs and the stone wall would be capped under the aqueduct: the variant's case never arises.
issues.required_change: E-V7-2 adds: '; and (4)'s "capped beneath the standing deck at its soffit; no gate on the deck, and a gate VS4 would make inside the raised way's under-deck strip, or within `raised.supportClearM` of a support, moves along the trace to the nearest clear point, the track following it" -> "its top as §2.7's laws, law 1 (7), give it (capped beneath a road deck's standing span, an aqueduct capping none); no gate on the deck, and a gate VS4 makes placed by §2.7's laws (law 1 (5), law 2 (a), law 3: off a road deck's under-deck strip and `raised.supportClearM` off a support's ring, under an aqueduct's arch only where the crossing is over and every span over it clears it), the track following it"'.
